PURSUIT
Marinésio Pereira da Silva, an attendant at the Esso station belonging to Humberto Pessoa, said he was just finishing watching a film on television, “around one in the morning, when the Caravan arrived with the four elderly people, terrified, trembling and almost without speech, saying they were being pursued by three flying saucers. That was when
[...]
saucers. When one of the saucers stopped above the car, the engine and radio immediately stopped working. At that moment the vehicle's occupants panicked, but a bus appeared, the saucer rose and the car started working again. It happened very near the station, and they arrived terrified, afraid to continue their journey.”
Milton says he also saw the saucer. “It was a wonderful light; it looked like a rainbow. At the time I felt no fear at all. In fact, I even wanted them to come down here for a beer so I could have a chat with them.”

source_image_corrections.translation: They use the Instamatic system, patented by Kodak. The system itself is quite practical. There is no need to position the film inside the camera. The film and winding mechanism are incorporated into a single-piece cartridge. When the costs are added up, it is relatively expensive. It takes up the same space as a 35 mm film spool but provides far fewer exposures. It requires special cameras. There is a whole range of models for this system. The simplest cameras, in the domestic Instamatic class, should be avoided for the same reasons given against box cameras. Other limitations: they do not allow double exposures or the simultaneous use of two rolls of film.

3.2.6. CONSIDERAÇÕES FINAIS SOBRE DISPOSITIVOS E MECANISMOS DE UMA CÂMARA
Uma boa câmara fotográfica deve ter, no mínimo, um telêmetro e um fotômetro. Mas pode-se considerar razoável uma câmara que tenha fotômetro mas não o telêmetro e vice-versa. A falta do telêmetro obriga-nos a cálculos de distância, a do fotômetro a cálculos de luminosidade. Uma e outra dessas deficiências podem ser sanadas pela aquisição de um fotômetro ou telêmetro avulsos. Isto vale para quem tem câmaras antigas.

3.2.6. FINAL CONSIDERATIONS ON CAMERA DEVICES AND MECHANISMS
A good camera should have at least a rangefinder and a light meter. A camera with a light meter but no rangefinder, or vice versa, can nevertheless be considered adequate. The absence of a rangefinder requires distance calculations, and the absence of a light meter requires brightness calculations. Either shortcoming can be remedied by obtaining a separate light meter or rangefinder. This applies to owners of older cameras.

O resultado final também inclui as cores que não o preto e o branco: cada uma delas é interpretada por uma tonalidade cinza correspondente. Para cada tipo de filme existem tabelas de correspondência entre cores e suas correspondentes tonalidades cinza captadas pelo filme.
Quanto à revelação, tanto para o negativo, como para as cópias, o processo compreende uma dupla de banhos químicos. O primeiro é o revelador, que faz aparecer a imagem registrada. O segundo é o fixador que fixa a referida imagem. Em outras palavras, o fixador impede a continuação das reações de fotólise dos sais de prata. Sem este banho, ou sendo o mesmo mal feito, a cópia — após alguns anos — começa a clarear, assumindo um tom acastanhado para, finalmente, esmaecer-se.
Os filmes preto-e-branco compreendem dois tipos principais: ortocromáticos e pancromáticos. Os primeiros cobrem todo o espectro visível, exceto o vermelho. Isto quer dizer: um objeto vermelho é registrado como branco, num filme ortocromático.
Nos filmes pancromáticos essa limitação foi contornada: são capazes de registrar também o vermelho segundo uma tonalidade de cinza.

image — negative — photograph
The final result also includes colors that are not black or white: each is represented by a corresponding shade of gray. For each type of film there are tables matching colors to the corresponding gray tones recorded by the film.
For both negatives and prints, development involves two chemical baths. The first is the developer, which makes the recorded image appear. The second is the fixer, which fixes that image. In other words, the fixer prevents further photolysis reactions of the silver salts. Without this bath, or if it is done poorly, after a few years the print begins to lighten, taking on a brownish tone and finally fading.
Black-and-white films comprise two main types: orthochromatic and panchromatic. The former cover the entire visible spectrum except red. This means that a red object is recorded as white on orthochromatic film.
In panchromatic films this limitation has been overcome: they can also record red as a shade of gray.
